corrected_proposal.title: Evercore acquired American Media; David Pecker was named chairman and CEO
corrected_proposal.description_short: Evercore acquired American Media, publisher of the National Enquirer and Star; David Pecker was appointed to lead the parent company.
corrected_proposal.description_medium: An Associated Press report carried by The Washington Post said Evercore Partners was buying American Media, publisher of the National Enquirer and Star, in a $300 million deal that also assumed debt. The Los Angeles Times reported that David Pecker, then chief executive of Hachette Filipacchi Magazines, was hired as American Media’s chairman and chief executive. The sources describe an Evercore-led acquisition and Pecker’s appointment; they do not establish a Trump-related purpose.
corrected_proposal.description_long: On February 17, 1999, The Washington Post published an Associated Press report saying Evercore Partners was buying American Media Inc., the publisher of the National Enquirer and Star. The report described a $300 million purchase and said Evercore would assume $470 million in debt. A Los Angeles Times report the same day said David Pecker, then head of Hachette Filipacchi Magazines, had been hired as American Media’s chairman and chief executive. The transaction was an Evercore-led acquisition of the parent publisher; Pecker was appointed to lead the company rather than shown as the individual buyer of the Enquirer. These reports correct the central ownership description. They do not establish that the paper was Mafia-owned, explain its earlier financing, or show a Trump-related purpose or connection in 1999. This card is limited to the corporate transaction and Pecker’s appointment as a contextual record. Any later political relationship involving Pecker requires its own evidence and should not be implied as the motive for this acquisition.
